newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean shares end firm in technical rebound.
newsitem.headline: Chilean shares end firm in technical rebound.

text.p: Chilean stocks recouped early losses to close slightly stronger in a technical rebound after the blue-chip IPSA index fell to close to 96.5 points, said traders.
"The market hit a floor at around 96.5 points midday and buyers started coming out," said one dealer.
The bolsa is seen opening with a mild rally supported by bargain-hunting after recent weakness, they said.
The IPSA index ended up 0.15 percent at 97.05 points. The general IGPA index gained 0.02 percent to 5,295.74 points amid turnover of 8.5 billion pesos.
Electricity stocks, which account for a 40 percent weighting in the IPSA index, firmed after falling sharply in recent weeks on concerns over sharp price cuts by regulators, said traders.
Enersis ended up 0.52 percent at 240-3/4 pesos while Endesa gained 0.3 percent to 252-1/4 pesos.
Investors are looking to a court case starting Tuesday brought by power companies who are locked in battle with the government over the new rates.
The government has already slashed generating rates by 11 percent and is widely expected to cut distribution tariffs by a similar amount, said analysts.
Other rises included pulp producer Copec which has been hammered in the last week after reporting lower-than-expected third quarter earnings, said dealers.
The stock firmed as investors realized that the market had overreacted to the figures, they said.
Copec, Chile's largest cellulose producer, climbed 2.03 percent to 1,630 pesos.
Losers included winery Concha y Toro, down 2.3 percent at 170 pesos, steel-maker Cap, down 1.83 percent at 1,070 pesos and bottler Andina, which shed 0.43 percent at 2,320 pesos.
